```{r, include=FALSE}
library(highcharter)
hc_set_theme("hcrt", tooltip = list(valueDecimals = 2))
options(download.file.method = "libcurl")
```

Highcharter includes the official Highcharts series and feature modules in its
main bundle. They work directly with `highchart()`; no additional dependency is
needed. Stock Tools, its GUI and technical indicators are loaded by
`highchartstock()`.

Community plugins are kept separate because they are narrower and can interfere
with one another. Add one to an individual widget with `hc_add_dependency()`.

It should be noted that from time to time the plugins interfere with each
other so you must be careful in using them.


## Regression

This plugin was created by Ignacio Vazquez (https://github.com/phpepe) and
let you add a regression series to any existing series on your chart. Calculates
the r-squared value (coefficient of determination) and optionally prints it on
the legend. If Linear or Polynomial regression is selected, you can print
the equation on the legend.

```{r}
library(highcharter)

data(penguins, package = "palmerpenguins")

penguins <- penguins[complete.cases(penguins), ]

hchart(
  penguins,
  "scatter",
  name = "Penguins",
  # opacity = 0.35,
  hcaes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = bill_length_mm),
  regression = TRUE,
  regressionSettings = list(
    type = "polynomial",
    dashStyle = "ShortDash",
    color = "skyblue",
    order = 3,
    lineWidth = 5,
    name = "%eq | r2: %r",
    hideInLegend = FALSE
  )
) |>
  hc_add_dependency("plugins/highcharts-regression.js")
```

Even you can get a regression for each series/group.

```{r}
hchart(
  penguins,
  "scatter",
  hcaes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = bill_length_mm, group = species),
  regression = TRUE
) |>
  hc_colors(c("#d35400", "#2980b9", "#2ecc71")) |>
  hc_add_dependency("plugins/highcharts-regression.js")
```

A detail of the each parameter can be found in the github page of this plugin:
https://github.com/streamlinesocial/highcharts-regression#regression-settings.

## Grouped Categories

Home page: http://blacklabel.github.io/grouped_categories/

Let's try an example:

```{r}
library(purrr) # map function to make grouped categories argument
library(dplyr) # for select function

data(mpg, package = "ggplot2")

mpgg <- mpg |>
  filter(!manufacturer %in% c("volkswagen", "chevrolet")) |>
  filter(class %in% c("compact", "midsize", "subcompact")) |>
  count(class, manufacturer, name = "count") |>
  arrange(class, manufacturer) |>
  mutate(position = row_number() - 1L)

categories_grouped <- mpgg |>
  select(class, manufacturer) |>
  group_by(name = class) |>
  summarise(categories = list(as.list(manufacturer))) |>
  list_parse()

hchart(
  mpgg,
  "column",
  name = "Cars",
  hcaes(x = position, y = count)
) |>
  hc_xAxis(
    # specify the grouped categories
    categories = categories_grouped,
    title = list(text = NULL),
    # styling a little bit
    labels = list(distance = 0, style = list(fontSize = "10px"))
  ) |>
  hc_add_dependency("plugins/grouped-categories.js")
```

## Draggable-points

More details in https://api.highcharts.com/highcharts/plotOptions.series.dragDrop.

```{r}
set.seed(123)

df <- tibble(
  x = runif(10),
  y = runif(10),
  z = runif(10),
  name = paste("cat", 1:10)
)

hchart(
  df,
  "bubble",
  hcaes(x = x, y = y),
  # showInLegend = TRUE,
  name = "You can move the points",
  cursor = "move",
  dragDrop = list(
    draggableX = TRUE,
    draggableY = TRUE
  )
)


df$x <- NULL

hchart(
  df,
  "column",
  hcaes(x = name, y = y),
  showInLegend = TRUE,
  name = "You can move the points only Yaxis direction",
  cursor = 'ns-resize',
  dragDrop = list(
    draggableY = TRUE
  )
)
```

## Pattern fills

Pattern fill is an official Highcharts module, already included in the shared
bundle. It belongs here as a bundled extension: there is no need to add a module
dependency. Community plugins such as Motion and Regression remain optional.
See https://www.highcharts.com/blog/tutorials/pattern-fills/.

Example taken from https://jsfiddle.net/gh/get/library/pure/highcharts/highcharts/tree/master/samples/highcharts/series/pattern-fill-area.

```{r}
# base chart without series
hc_fill <- highchart() |>
  hc_chart(type = 'area') |>
  hc_title(text = 'Pattern fills from the bundled module') |>
  hc_xAxis(
    categories = month.abb
  ) |>
  hc_plotOptions(
    area = list(
      fillColor = list(
        pattern = list(
          path = list(
            d = 'M 0 0 L 10 10 M 9 -1 L 11 1 M -1 9 L 1 11',
            strokeWidth = 3
          ),
          width = 10,
          height = 10,
          opacity = 0.4
        )
      )
    )
  )

# test with 2 series
hc_fill |>
  hc_add_series(
    data = c(29.9, 71.5, 106.4, 129.2, 144.0, 176.0, 135.6),
    color = '#88e',
    fillColor = list(
      pattern = list(
        color = '#11d'
      )
    )
  ) |>
  hc_add_series(
    data = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, 43.1, 95.6, 148.5, 216.4, 194.1, 95.6, 54.4),
    color = '#e88',
    fillColor = list(
      pattern = list(
        color = '#d11'
      )
    )
  )
```

## Gantt schedules

Use `hchart(tasks, "gantt")` for a schedule with dependencies. See the
[complete Gantt example](showcase.html#gantt-schedules) for a release plan with progress bars.

## Motion

Motion is a [community plugin by Lars Cabrera](https://github.com/larsac07/Motion-Highcharts-Plugin),
not an official Highcharts module. Its JavaScript ships separately in the R
package; `hc_motion()` attaches it to this chart. It is not part of the shared
Highcharts bundle.

Watch life expectancy change across continents from 1952 to 2007. Each point
carries a sequence of population-weighted means from the local Gapminder data.
The fixed value scale makes the changes comparable. Press Play or drag the
year slider; the chart begins in 1952.

```{r motion-life-expectancy}
library(dplyr)
data(gapminder, package = "gapminder")
history <- gapminder |>
  group_by(continent, year) |>
  summarise(lifeExp = weighted.mean(lifeExp, pop), .groups = "drop")
years <- sort(unique(history$year))
continents <- unique(as.character(history$continent))
points <- lapply(continents, function(continent) {
  values <- history[as.character(history$continent) == continent, ]
  values <- values[order(values$year), ]
  list(name = continent, y = values$lifeExp[1], sequence = values$lifeExp)
})

highchart() |>
  hc_chart(type = "bar", spacingBottom = 88) |>
  hc_title(text = "Longer lives, different trajectories") |>
  hc_subtitle(text = "Population-weighted life expectancy by continent") |>
  hc_xAxis(categories = continents) |>
  hc_yAxis(
    min = 25,
    max = 85,
    title = list(text = "Life expectancy (years)")
  ) |>
  hc_add_series(name = "Life expectancy", data = points, colorByPoint = TRUE) |>
  hc_tooltip(valueDecimals = 1, valueSuffix = " years") |>
  hc_motion(
    labels = as.character(years),
    startIndex = 0,
    magnet = list(step = 1),
    updateInterval = 900
  ) |>
  hc_credits(enabled = TRUE, position = list(y = -65)) |>
  hc_caption(
    text = "Source: Gapminder. The continent means are weighted by population."
  ) |>
  hc_size(height = 460)
```

## Chart language

Open the export menu on each chart to compare the same controls in Chilean
Spanish and French. Each widget captures the language in effect when it is
created. Restore the previous setting with `options(old)` after creating them.

```{r chart-language}
old <- hc_set_language("es-CL")
spanish <- hchart(AirPassengers) |> hc_exporting(enabled = TRUE)
hc_set_language("fr-FR")
french <- hchart(AirPassengers) |> hc_exporting(enabled = TRUE)
options(old)

htmltools::tagList(spanish, french)
```

## Optional community plugins

The official modules are already part of the generated bundle. These community
plugins remain optional:

- Motion adds a time slider with `hc_motion()`.
- Regression adds fitted curves with `hc_add_dependency("plugins/highcharts-regression.js")`.
- Grouped Categories adds nested axis labels.
- Draggable Legend lets readers reposition a legend.

For click-to-detail navigation, see [Drilldown](drilldown.html).
